question.text: Secular trends in an economy are best described as:

answer.text: Short-term patterns following weather or agricultural seasons lasting one year
Medium-term cyclical patterns lasting 2-6 years that eventually reverse
Long-term structural changes that occur once in 7-10 years and create displacement in goods or services produced or consumed
Daily price fluctuations in stock markets

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 100-101, secular trends refer to long-term change that creates displacement in goods or services consumed or produced. Such trends occur once in 7-10 years and are driven by factors such as technology, demographics, and cultural shifts. The Trap: Seasonal trends are annual and cyclical trends are typically 2-6 years and reversing. Only secular trends produce structural displacement. The source language is that secular trends 'occur once in 7-10 years', not that they necessarily last for that entire span. Note: Digitalization is a commonly cited example of a secular trend in the workbook, reshaping consumption patterns across multiple industries.
